Situation1: A serious situation has come up in the family, and the grandparent's presence is needed.
Expectation2: Perform maintenance and cleaning of the machines to ensure optimal performance
Situation2: A few machines are running hotter than normal after missing their last service window.
Story:
I sat at the kitchen table, my phone buzzing with messages from my daughter. She needed me—her voice trembled over the line, asking if I could come over and help with the kids. Something serious had happened, and my presence was needed, not just as a babysitter, but as the steady hand of a grandparent who could bring calm to the chaos. I looked at the clock, feeling the weight of family expectation settle on my shoulders.

But then my work phone rang. The plant manager’s voice was urgent: “A few machines are running hotter than normal. We missed the last service window, and if we don’t get them cleaned and checked today, we could be looking at a shutdown.” I knew what that meant—lost production, angry clients, and a team depending on me to keep things running smoothly.

My heart pounded as I stared at the two phones, each demanding my attention. I could picture my grandchildren’s anxious faces, needing comfort, and at the same time, I could almost hear the hum of the machines, warning me of trouble. I felt torn, the expectations of both worlds pulling me in opposite directions, and I didn’t know which call to answer first.
